question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡{x}^{3})-\frac{3}{4}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{({x}^{3})}^{2}}\cdot ({x}^{3})^{′}-\frac{3}{4}(4{x}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{6}}\cdot 3{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3} \\  & =3{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{1-{x}^{6}}-x).\end{aligned}
$$
